s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neck pain with radiating pain and neurological deficits
salient_findings: Electrical pain radiating to the left hand
Weakness in fine movements and weak grip of the left hand
Atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles of the left hand
key_facts: 6-month history of progressive neck pain
Pain radiates to the left hand
Numbness in the C8–T1 dermatomes
Weakness in fine movements of the left hand
Weak grip of the left hand
Atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles of the left hand
Motor testing of the left hand revealed muscle strength of 3/5
Marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra on CT
Lesion involves the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments
Lesion does not significantly compromise the thecal sac

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of progressive neck pain with radiating pain and neurological deficits, and the imaging findings of osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra

shortlist.label: Osteoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the imaging findings of osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, and the clinical presentation of progressive neck pain with radiating pain and neurological deficits

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of the osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, and the clinical presentation of progressive neck pain with radiating pain and neurological deficits

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of progressive neck pain with radiating pain and neurological deficits, and the imaging findings of a lesion involving the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments

shortlist.label: Plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of the osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, and the clinical presentation of progressive neck pain with radiating pain and neurological deficits, although less common than other options

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with progressive neck pain radiating to the left hand, numbness in the C8–T1 dermatomes, and marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra is consistent with a giant cell tumor, which is known to cause bone destruction and neurological symptoms due to its location and potential to compress nearby structures.

rejected.label: Osteoblastoma
rejected.why: Osteoblastoma is less likely due to its typically smaller size and less aggressive nature compared to the extensive osteolysis and collapse seen in this case.

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Aneurysmal bone cysts are often characterized by a soap-bubble appearance on imaging, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Chordomas are typically midline lesions and often involve the clivus or sacrum, which does not match the T1 vertebra location in this patient.

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: Plasmacytoma would more likely present with systemic symptoms such as anemia, renal failure, or hypercalcemia, which are not mentioned in the vignette.
